Duck Detector provides reference signals only. %1$s Always combine the app\'s output with manual verification, upstream evidence, and your own risk assessment before taking action.

By using Duck Detector, you agree to the following terms:

1. Purpose of use
This application is designed solely for educational and personal security-assessment purposes. It helps users understand the security status of their own devices.

2. No warranty
This application is provided "as is" without any warranties, express or implied. The developers do not guarantee the accuracy, completeness, or reliability of detection results.

3. User responsibility
You are solely responsible for how you use this application and any consequences that may arise from its use.

4. Compliance with laws
You agree to use this application in compliance with all applicable local, national, and international laws and regulations.

IMPORTANT NOTICE:

1. Detection limitations
Duck Detector uses various methods to detect device security status, but no detection method is 100% accurate. Results should be considered indicators rather than definitive assessments.

2. False positives and false negatives
The application may produce false positives or false negatives. Always use professional security tools and your own verification for comprehensive assessment.

3. No liability
The developers, contributors, and distributors of Duck Detector shall not be held liable for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, or consequential damages arising from the use or inability to use this application.

4. Third-party services
TEE revocation checks use a built-in snapshot by default. If you allow online revocation refresh, the app may contact the Google attestation revocation endpoint. Security scans themselves still run locally on your device, and detector findings are not intentionally uploaded as scan telemetry.

Privacy summary: Security checks run locally on your device. Detector findings are not intentionally uploaded as scan telemetry. After startup choices are complete, the app contacts GitHub once per cold start to check Nightly update metadata. If you turn on GitHub acceleration, these requests go through the third-party gh-proxy.com service instead.
